verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Both interpolation inequalities are stated verbatim, with identical exponents: B_R = ‖φ_R^4 w‖6 is comparisonLpNorm 6 (φ^4 • w), ‖w‖2 is comparisonLpNorm 2 w, and the exponent pairs (1/2, 1/2) for the L³ bound and (1/4, 3/4) for the L⁴ bound match the paper factor for factor; the Lean also adds the membership conclusion (MemLp) that the paper leaves implicit. Two gaps, both packaging. First, the Lean inequalities hold for any φ ≥ 0 that is a.e.-strongly-measurable — no upper bound of one is required, as the file docstring notes — so they are stated more generally than for φ_R. Second, the first link of the paper's chain, ‖φ_R³w‖_3 ≤ ‖φ_R²w‖_3, is not a named declaration: it is one line from cutoff_le_one (0 ≤ φ_R ≤ 1, so φ_R³ ≤ φ_R² pointwise) together with lpNorm_mono_of_norm_le. The Lean's own pressure-flux route never needs it — it reduces the cutoff power pointwise instead (PressureFluxTest.norm_r_le bounds the test by (8L)‖φ³w‖ directly), and cutoff_interpolation_three is used only at WeightedInterpolation.lean:204 inside cutoff_transport_bound, not on the pressure route.
